body:
### Summary

Since v1.15.0 a string-form lifecycle script with more than one word in it gets mangled
before it reaches the container. Most fail with `DevContainerScriptsFailed`; some quietly
run half the command.

The command is built correctly as argv, then flattened back into a string and handed to a
shell, which re-splits it:

```
built:    ["/bin/sh", "-c", "mkdir /tmp/zed-repro"]
executed: sh -c "/bin/sh -c mkdir /tmp/zed-repro"
```

`sh -c` takes only the next single word as its script, so that runs bare `mkdir` with
`/tmp/zed-repro` demoted to `$0`.

The [spec](https://containers.dev/implementors/json_reference/#lifecycle-scripts) has
string-form commands running in `/bin/sh` and suggests `&&` for chaining.

### Reproduction steps

1. A `devcontainer.json` with a two-word `postCreateCommand`:

```json
{
  "image": "debian:12",
  "postCreateCommand": "mkdir /tmp/zed-repro"
}
```

2. Open the folder in a dev container.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the container starts, then setup fails and `/tmp/zed-repro` is never created:

```
ERROR [dev_container::docker] Command produced a non-successful output. StdErr:
ERROR [recent_projects::remote_servers] Failed to start dev container: DevContainerUpFailed("Failed with nested error: DevContainerScriptsFailed")
```

`docker events` confirms what went in:

```
exec_create: sh -c /bin/sh -c mkdir /tmp/zed-repro
```

Running that directly:

```
$ docker exec c sh -c "/bin/sh -c mkdir /tmp/zed-repro"
mkdir: missing operand
Try 'mkdir --help' for more information.
$ echo $?
1
```

**Expected:** `/tmp/zed-repro` exists and the container attaches.

| `postCreateCommand` | result |
|---|---|
| `true` | works — single word, so the boundary loss is a no-op |
| `mkdir /tmp/zed-repro` | exit 1, `mkdir: missing operand`, nothing created |
| `echo hello && echo world` | **exit 0**, prints only `world` — `echo hello` became bare `echo` |

The last is the worst: setup looks like it succeeded.

### Where it goes wrong

`LifecycleScript::shell_command` builds the three argv elements the spec asks for
(`devcontainer_json.rs:344`):

```rust
vec!["/bin/sh".to_string(), "-c".to_string(), script.to_string()]
```

`run_docker_exec` joins them back together with spaces
([`docker.rs:377-386`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/dev_container/src/docker.rs#L377)):

```rust
command.arg("sh");

let mut inner_program_script: Vec<String> =
    vec![inner_command.get_program().display().to_string()];
let mut args: Vec<String> = inner_command
    .get_args()
    .map(|arg| arg.display().to_string())
    .collect();
inner_program_script.append(&mut args);
command.args(&["-c", &inner_program_script.join(" ")]);
```

`command_to_shell_string` (`devcontainer_manifest.rs:3362`) builds the `postStartCommand`
marker script the same way, so I'd expect `postStartCommand` to be affected too.

### Why it surfaced in v1.15.0

The `join(" ")` dates from #52338 (1 Apr), but string commands were parsed with
`args.split(" ")` back then, and split-then-join is the identity. #60792 (31 Jul) replaced
that with a spec-correct `/bin/sh -c <script>` — which looks right, but it removed the
cancellation while the join stayed. The one test over this path passes
`Command::new("true")`, the single shape the join is lossless for.

### Suggested fix

Quote each part on the way out. `devcontainer_manifest.rs` already has a helper that
may be an option for this:

```rust
fn shell_single_quote(value: &str) -> String {
    format!("'{}'", value.replace('\'', "'\\''"))
}
```

Applying it in `run_docker_exec` and `command_to_shell_string` would keep the boundaries.
Or drop the extra `sh -c` and pass the inner argv straight to `docker exec`.

### Test coverage

`run_docker_exec` builds and runs the command in one step, so the argv isn't observable
from a test. Splitting the construction out into a `create_docker_exec(...)`, alongside
the existing `create_docker_inspect` and friends, would make it assertable in the style of
`should_create_docker_inspect_command`. Shapes worth covering:

| input | why it matters |
|---|---|
| `true` | single word — the shape covered today |
| `mkdir /tmp/x` | operand demoted to `$0` |
| `echo a && echo b` | operator chaining, which the spec suggests |
| `git config user.name 'A B'` | quoted argument containing a space |
| `echo "it's"` | single quote in the value — exercises the escaping |
| `["yarn", "install"]` | array form should keep executing *without* a shell |

`command_to_shell_string` goes through the same join.

### Zed version and system specs

- Zed: 1.16.1+stable.343 (eb8e1c8)
- macOS 26.5.2, arm64
- Docker 29.7.2 (Docker Desktop)

comments.body:
Workaround:
set a "postStartCommand" as a simple script file and in there it works:
```
 "postStartCommand": ".devcontainer/post-start"
```

That workaround works, make sure to +x that file.

The bug still prevents me from opening the Pytorch devcontainer, so I do think it's worth fixing: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/142552d4b176930839b7df5f8f95963c2ab2c41b/.devcontainer/cuda/devcontainer.json#L26
Ran into this as well. Left details in [the PR](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/63034).
